title: Taiwanese Student Association at UC Santa Barbara
content_html:
The Taiwanese Student Association (TSA) at UC Santa Barbara is a non-profit, non-political, student-led organization dedicated to promoting and celebrating Taiwanese culture on campus. The organization is listed among Asian Pacific Islander student organizations by both UCSB’s Office of Undergraduate Admissions and the Educational Opportunity Program’s Asian Resource Center, and maintains an active presence on Shoreline, the university’s official student engagement platform. Its mission, as stated on its website, is to enrich students’ social and cultural collegiate experience among those who share a common interest in Taiwan.

The TSA primarily serves Taiwanese international students at UCSB, offering orientation resources, community support, and programming to help members get acclimated to life in Santa Barbara. The organization communicates in both English and Mandarin Chinese — including through its Instagram account (@ucsb_tsa) and email — and has held in-person information sessions in Taiwan for incoming students. It coexists on campus alongside the Taiwanese American Student Association (TASA), which focuses on the Taiwanese American experience; the TSA’s own FAQ notes that TSA “primarily serves as a community for Taiwanese students at UCSB.”
